activities.caption: one line of the marketing summary is wrong
activities.name: cmKodakSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary of what marketing is for is wrong. Find it.
lines: Marketing is identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer needs profitably
Market size tells you the prize; market share tells you your standing
Share tends to compound: bigger firms buy cheaper, advertise harder, appear in more places
Kodak's film market shrank because people stopped wanting pictures
The market is a moving photograph that must be re-taken continuously
config.correction: Kodak's film market shrank because the job moved to a different technology — people still wanted pictures.
config.why: Incomes rise, tastes shift, technology substitutes, new competitors appear — which is why the photograph must be re-taken continuously.

activities.caption: file each market by its structure
activities.name: cmStructureBuckets

config.prompt: Four structures, one shelf of examples. File each:
config.why: Structure decides how much freedom any player has: identical products forbid pricing power, differentiation earns it, and a few big players compete by watchfulness.

activities.caption: one shelf, three segments — pair reason with product
activities.name: cmToothpasteMatch

config.prompt: The toothpaste shelf's three segments — pair each with what it is buying:
config.why: A 60-year-old and a 16-year-old may be in the same segment; two 35-year-olds may be in different ones — segments are discovered in why-questions, not age brackets.

activities.anchor: is the choice of which segments to serve
activities.caption: run the targeting decision
activities.name: cmTargetBranch

config.root: The segments are cut and scored. Now choose how widely to serve — each strategy carries its own risks.

start.text: The firm's product could technically serve everyone. What is the targeting call?

choices.label: Mass marketing — one offer for everyone
choices.feedback: The utilities-and-table-salt play: reach is huge, differentiation thin, and pricing power with it.

choices.label: Niche marketing — serve one segment deeply
choices.feedback: Specialist running shoes for overpronators: depth, loyalty, and a defensible premium.

choices.label: Concentrated — dominate a small pond first
choices.feedback: Win the pond before trying the lake: focus now, expansion later.

mass.text: A rival starts out-positioning you in one profitable sub-group. Response?

choices.label: Position on price and scale
choices.feedback: A real position — if the cost structure can keep the promise true.

choices.label: Ignore the sub-group; the mass is the strategy
choices.feedback: Risky: niches are where concentrated entrants dig in first.

niche.text: The niche rewards you — until a giant bothers to copy. Build the switching costs that make the position defensible.

concentrated.text: Dominance in a small pond funds the next expansion — on your own terms.

position.text: Differentiation buys pricing power — that is why branding exists at all.

ignore.text: The sub-group's margin funds someone else's beachhead — watch that gap.

config.why: Evaluated on size and growth, accessibility, competition already in the segment, and fit with what you are actually good at.

activities.caption: true or false — positioning versus slogans
activities.name: cmTaglineJudge

statements.s: The tagline is the last 1 per cent of positioning; the first 99 is the operations that make the claim true.
statements.why: Positioning lives or dies on a unique selling point a competitor cannot cheaply copy.

statements.s: A budget airline positioning on the lowest fare must actually run single aircraft types, secondary airports, no-refund tickets and fast turnarounds.
statements.why: Every cost decision exists to keep the promise cheap.

statements.s: A luxury brand claiming craftsmanship can skip constraining supply and sweating the finish.
statements.why: The claim must be made true — otherwise it is a lie customers discover.

statements.s: Positioning operations cannot support becomes, once discovered, the positioning.
statements.why: Discovered lies are remembered longer than slogans.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the research toolkit
activities.name: cmResearchCloze

config.text: Primary research is gathered first-hand; secondary research %%0%% what exists. A %%1%% sample gives everyone an equal chance of selection, while quota sampling fills preset category quotas. The cardinal rule of startup-era research: ask about the %%2%%, not the future.
config.hint: One word names the unbiased sampling method; one word is the time direction that yields evidence instead of polite fiction.

activities.caption: call the precision — what 1,000 respondents buy
activities.name: cmSampleEstimate

config.prompt: A random sample of 1,000 respondents — roughly what margin of error does it carry?
config.why: Roughly 1 ÷ √n: 1,000 gives about ±3.2, 400 about ±5 — and since cost follows √n, doubling precision quadruples the sample.
config.context: A product decision hinging on 68 versus 71 per cent needs a bigger sample, not a bolder slide.

activities.anchor: if you could no longer use this product
activities.caption: drop the marker on the fit threshold
activities.name: cmFitPlace

config.prompt: Sean Ellis's test: what share answering 'very disappointed' marks a product as essential to a core group? Place the marker:
config.why: About 40 per cent — below it, refocus on whatever sub-group scores highest rather than advertise harder; retention is the other tell, and fit is perishable.
